b.e43effd6e3:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.a8f191c38e:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Ioánnem
<r>Ioannes 7:1-13</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Ambulábat Iesus in Galilǽam: non enim volébat in Iudǽam ambuláre, quia quærébant eum Iudǽi interfícere. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
<r>Tractatus 28 in Ioannem</r>
<c>I</c>n isto Evangélii capítulo, fratres, Dóminus noster Iesus Christus secúndum hóminem se plúrimum commendávit fídei nostræ. Etenim semper hoc egit dictis et factis suis, ut Deus credátur et homo: Deus qui nos fecit, homo qui nos quæsívit: Deus cum Patre semper, homo nobíscum ex témpore. Non enim quǽreret quem fécerat, nisi fíeret ipse quod fécerat. Verum hoc mementóte, et de córdibus vestris nolíte dimíttere: sic esse Christum hóminem factum, ut non destíterit Deus esse.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus meus es tu, ne discédas a me:
* Quóniam tribulátio próxima est, et non est qui ádiuvet.
<r>℣.</r> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam tribulátio próxima est, et non est qui ádiuvet.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to John
<r>John 7:1-13</r>
<c>A</c>t that time: Jesus walked in Galilee; for he would not walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him. And so on.

Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop <n>of Hippo.</n>
<r>28th Tract on John</r>
<c>I</c>n this chapter of the Gospel, my brethren, our Lord Jesus Christ hath much commended Himself unto our faith, as touching His Manhood. At the same time, His words and works were alway such as to give us to believe that He is both God and Man, yea, that God Who made us, and that Man Who hath sought us, yea, God the Son, Who, as touching His Godhead, is alway with the Father, <n>John i. 18; iii. 13,</n> and, as touching His Manhood, hath been with us in time. <n>Matth. i. 23.</n> For He had not sought the work of His hands unless He had been made His own work. <n>John i. 14.</n> Keep this well in mind, and let your hearts never forget it, namely, that Christ was not made Man so as to cease to be God.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Thou art my God; be not far from me, for trouble is near;
* For there is none to help.
<r>℣.</r> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me.
<r>℟.</r> For trouble is near; for there is none to help.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>H</c>e, Who made the Manhood, took It into that Godhead Which is His from everlasting to everlasting. While therefore He lay hid in the Manhood, we must not think that He had suffered any lessening of power, but that He was giving example to our weakness. When He willed it, He was taken; when He willed it, He was put to death. <n>John x. 18.</n> But, since He was to have members, that is, His faithful people, who would not have that power over their lives which He, our God, had over His, He hid Himself, He concealed Himself, as if it were to escape being put to death, to show what should be done by those His members in whom He should dwell.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>hrist is not the Head of His Church in such sense that He is not in her Body; but the whole Christ is in the Head, and the whole Christ is in the Body. That, then, which His members are is Himself, though That Which He is, That are not therefore His members. For if His members had not been indeed His Own, how had He said unto Saul, <n>Acts ix. 4</n>: Why persecutest thou Me? since Saul was not persecuting Him in Himself, but in His members, that is, in His faithful ones which were upon earth. He said not: Why persecutest thou My holy ones, nor: My servants, no, nor yet called He them by that more honourable name “My brethren”, but, “Why persecutest thou Me?”; that is, the members of My Body, whose Head I am.

<c>T</c>hirty years among us dwelling,

On the cross the Lamb is lifted,
Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

Vinegar, and spear, and reed;
From that holy body broken
Blood and water forth proceed:
Earth, and stars, and sky, and ocean,
By that flood from stain are free.

<h>F</h>aithful cross! above all other,
One and only noble tree!
None in foliage, none in blossom,
None in fruit thy peers may be;
Sweetest wood and sweetest iron!

Thy relaxing sinews bend;

This world's ransom to uphold;
For a shipwrecked race preparing
Harbour, like the ark of old;
With the sacred blood anointed
From the smitten Lamb that rolled.

Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.

<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>arch 17th 2027, the 9th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Ireland, the holy Confessor Patrick, Bishop [of Armagh,] the first who there preached the Gospel of Christ, and who was famous for great miracles and works of power, [in the year 464.]
<h>A</h>t Jerusalem, holy Joseph of Arimathea, the honourable councillor, the disciple of the Lord, who took down His Body from the cross and laid it in his own new tomb.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander and Theodore.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria are commemorated many holy martyrs, who were seized by the worshippers of Serapis, and because they would not worship that idol were cruelly murdered by them, in the time of the Emperor Theodosius, who presently afterward sent a rescript to destroy the temple of Serapis.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy martyr Paul, who was burnt under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus for defending the honouring of holy images.
<h>A</h>t Chalons [-sur-Saône,] in Gaul, holy Agricola, Bishop of that see, [in the year 580.]
<h>A</h>t Nivelles, in Brabant, the holy Virgin Gertrude, the daughter of an illustrious race, who despised this world, and busied herself all her life in holy deeds, so that she won to be espoused to Christ in heaven, [in the year 659.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.cbd3e449aa:
<h>Canticle: Magnificat</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Go ye up unto this Feast; * I go not up (yet) unto this Feast, for My time is not yet full come.
<r>Canticle of the Blessed Virgin</r>
<r>Luke 1:46-55</r>
§00.83742356bc
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Go ye up unto this Feast; I go not up (yet) unto this Feast, for My time is not yet full come.
b.87052d456d:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>a nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, perseverántem in tua voluntáte famulátum: ut in diébus nostris et mérito et número pópulus tibi sérviens augeátur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.e25e097836:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee to give us grace to endure to the end in doing of thy will, that in our days thy people which serve thee may have increase, both as touching bettering of their works, and multiplying of their numbers.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.0dbe0cbb8f:
<h>Canticum: Nunc dimittis</h>
<r>Ant.</r> O Rex glorióse inter Sanctos tuos, qui semper es laudábilis et tamen ineffábilis: tu in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos Deus noster: ut in die iudícii nos collocáre dignéris inter Sanctos et Eléctos tuos, Rex benedícte.

b.ba99451005:
<h>Canticle: Nunc dimittis</h>
<r>Ant.</r> O glorious King among thy Saints, who art ever to be praised and yet art ineffable: thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy holy name is called upon us: forsake us not, O our God; that in the day of judgement thou mayest vouchsafe to place us among thy Saints and thine Elect, O blessed King.

<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>N</c>ostra tibi, Dómine, quǽsumus, sint accépta ieiúnia: quæ nos et expiándo, grátia tua dignos effíciant, et ad remédia perdúcant ætérna.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.980383bd4e:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>ord, we beseech thee, that this our Fast may be acceptable in thy sight, and may, through thy blessing, effectually work in us, making us meet here to receive thy grace and hereafter the everlasting glory which Thou hast promised.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
